ledger.note: 1206: Qutb ud-Din Aibak is crowned at Lahore. 'He informally ascended the throne on 25 June 1206' at Qasr-e-Humayun, Lahore; the Mamluk page: he 'became the sultan of Delhi, establishing the Mamluk dynasty' after Muhammad of Ghor's assassination, and the infobox says 'Established: 1206'. His Ghurid overlord Mahmud conferred the parasol in 1208-1209; Muhammad's page has Aibak declare 'independence in 1208'.
1210: the seat moves from Lahore to Badaun. Infobox 'Badayun (1210-1214)'; Aibak died on 4 November 1210 playing chaugan at Lahore.

1211: Qabacha takes Lahore. 'Qabacha had captured Lahore in 1211' (Iltutmish page); the page later has Yildiz 'displace' Qabacha from Lahore (no year) and Qabacha regain it after Tarain, until Iltutmish 'captured Lahore in the winter of 1216-1217'. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: thin finding: Lahore was drawn Mamluk 1210-1215.]
1214: Delhi becomes the capital. Infobox 'Delhi (from 1214)'; the Iltutmish page has him 'set up his capital at Delhi' on dethroning Aram Shah in 1211.

1210s: Bihar. The Iltutmish page says Bihar was captured 'in the 1210s' (and gives Malik Jani as governor after the 1225 Bengal expedition); the year is mine, 1215 as the middle of the decade, and the Cliopatria shape reaches it only in 1227. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: Bihar now appears in mamluk-dynasty_1215 and in the Bihar addition to mamluk-dynasty_1216.]
25 January 1216: Iltutmish defeats Yildiz at Tarain. The page dates the battle 'to 25 January 1216'; Yildiz 'was later killed at Badaun'.
1216: Yildiz is defeated and taken at Tarain.

Winter 1216-1217: Iltutmish takes Lahore. He 'captured Lahore in the winter of 1216-1217' and set his son Nasiruddin Mahmud over it. [Reviewer sa-04-a: counterpart changed from Yildiz of Ghazni: the Iltutmish page says Yildiz 'displaced Qabacha from Lahore', and after Tarain Iltutmish 'did not immediately assert his control over the Punjab region, and Qabacha regained control of Lahore'; 'Iltutmish then captured Lahore in the winter of 1216-1217']

region.text: the Punjab between Lahore and Multan

ledger.note: 4 May 1228: Uch falls after a three-month siege; Qabacha drowns himself in the Indus on 26 May.
1228: Multan and Uch. Iltutmish captured Uch 'on 4 May 1228'; 'Multan and Uch were placed under Iltutmish's governors' and his authority reached Makran and the Arabian Sea coast (no frontier given).

region.text: the sultanate of Iltutmish at the investiture

ledger.note: 18 February 1229: the caliph's deed of investiture reaches Delhi. 'In 1228, the new Caliph sent the ambassador back to Delhi with robes of honour'; 'On 18 February 1229, the embassy arrived in Delhi with a deed of investiture' (Iltutmish page). A nominal allegiance (no tribute on the page), the 'Allegiance of Delhi Sultanate to Abbasid Caliphate' relation of Cliopatria (1210-1259), which the abbasid-caliphate dossier opens in 1210 at confidence 1 and should move to 1229; the renderer may prefer to treat it as an association. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: investiture missing from the ledger.]
12 December 1232: Gwalior. Iltutmish besieged it in 1231 and captured it 'on 12 December 1232'.
c. 1233: Kalinjar attacked. Under Malik Nusratuddin Taisi 'Kalinjar was attacked and plundered for about 50 days, around 1233-34'.
c. 1234: the Kalinjar raid ends without annexation.

1234-35: Iltutmish's army occupies Bhilsa. 'Iltutmish's army occupied Bhilsa, and destroyed a temple' during the raid of 1234-35 on 'the Paramara-controlled cities of Bhilsa and Ujjain'; the Paramara dynasty page (paramara-dynasty ledger 1233) has 'Iltutmish captured Bhilsa during 1233-34', and 1234 is the year both pages share. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: Bhilsa was drawn as a raid that 'adds no land'.]

1234: Iltutmish raids Ujjain. 'Iltutmish raided the Paramara-controlled cities of Bhilsa and Ujjain in 1234-35', damaging the Mahakaleshwar temple at Ujjain; for the Paramara territory he 'made little effort to annex' it. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: Bhilsa split off as an occupation, Ujjain stays a raid (contest).]
1235: the Ujjain raid ends; no land is annexed ('made little effort to annex the Paramara territory').
By 1239 (bridge): Devapala regains Bhilsa. The Iltutmish page is silent on the end of the occupation; the year mirrors paramara-dynasty ledger 1239 ('Devapala regained it'; Devapala reigned to 1239).

30 December 1241: the Mongols sack Lahore. 'on 30 December 1241, the Mongols under Munggetu butchered the town before withdrawing from the Delhi Sultanate' (Mongol invasions of India page, in the paragraph on the siege of Lahore); the Mamluk page puts the sack in Bahram's reign (1240-1242) without a year. [Repair sa-04-a, thin finding: the Lahore sack was 'c. 1241' at confidence 1.]

union.text: Rarh
Varendra

ledger.note: 1243: the Odia army moves on Bengal. 'Forces moved toward Bengal in 1242-1243 CE'; Tughril Tughan 'launched a counterattack' by 1244. Mirror of eastern-ganga-kingdom ledger 1243. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: the Odia war on Mamluk Bengal was missing; contest added with the occupation.]

1244: Odia forces occupy Rarh and Gauda of Mamluk Bengal. 'In 1244 CE, the victorious Odia forces again seized two provinces of Varendra and Rarh'; 'Rarh and Gauda remained occupied by the Odia forces' (Narasingha Deva I page, no year for the second sentence). The Eastern Ganga dynasty page has only 'advanced to Varendra as far as Lakhnawati in 1245' and is silent on 1244 and 1247, so the Narasingha page is the source (the reviewer named the Eastern Ganga page). Region as eastern-ganga-kingdom ledger 1244. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: occupation of Rarh and Gauda missing.]

1247 (bridge): the occupation of Rarh and Gauda is taken to end. 'In 1247 CE, an able new Muslim military commander, lkhtiyar-ud-Din Yuzbak, was appointed as the governor of Bengal'; the page does not say when the Odia occupation ended. Mirror of eastern-ganga-kingdom ledger 1247.

union.text: Rarh
Varendra

ledger.note: 1247: Yuzbak is appointed governor of Bengal 'to free Bengal from Odia forces'; Paramardi Dev was killed in the fighting. The page gives no later date. Mirror of eastern-ganga-kingdom ledger 1247.
1247: Balban puts down a rising in Kalinjar. 'In 1247, Balban suppressed a rising of the Chandela Chief of Kalinjar.'
1247: the Kalinjar rising is suppressed.

February 1258 (bridge): the allegiance ends with the caliphate. The Iltutmish page is silent on the end; the date mirrors abbasid-caliphate's vassal_end (February 1258); Cliopatria's relation runs to 1259.

1275: Bengal revolts. 'When the governor of Bengal, Tughral Tughan Khan, revoked the authority of Delhi in 1275'; Balban sent the governor of Awadh and a second army, both failed, and then marched with a third that killed Tughral.

1281: Tughral is defeated and killed. 'Balban himself invaded Bengal in 1281'; 'Tughan was defeated and killed in the battle'; the page closes 'the separatist Mamluk ruling of Bengal ended in 1281' (Tughral Tughan Khan page, which gives no year for the revolt; the Balban page has 1275). Bughra Khan was put in charge of Bengal (no year). [Repair sa-04-a, thin finding: c. 1280 (bridge, confidence 1) replaced by 1281 from the Tughral page.]

9 March 1285: Prince Muhammad dies fighting the Mongols. 'He perished in a battle against the Mongols on 9 March 1285' (Balban page; Mamluk page: 'the Battle of Beas River'). The Punjab frontier with the Mongols closes with the last dated battle of the reign. [Reviewer sa-04-a: source changed to the Balban page, which has 'perished in a battle against the Mongols on 9 March 1285'; the Mamluk page names the Battle of Beas River without a year]

ledger.counterpart: Bughra Khan's Bengal (Balbani rulers of Lakhnauti)
ledger.note: 1287: Bengal under Bughra Khan. After Balban's death on 13 January 1287 Bughra Khan, his second son and governor of Bengal, 'declared independence'. [Repair sa-04-a, reviewer finding: counterpart changed from sultanate-of-bengal, whose Cliopatria row runs 1344-1533; the Balban page says Bughra 'maintained' his independence 'for 40 years' (to about 1327). The words 'Balbani' and 'Lakhnauti' are the reviewer's labels; the page says only Bengal.]

1290: the Khalji Revolution ends the Mamluk dynasty. Jalal ud-Din Firuz Khalji, Qaiqabad's army commander, 'assumed power in the Khalji Revolution, thus ending the Mamluk dynasty and founding the Khalji dynasty' (infobox 1 February to 13 June 1290); Qaiqabad 'was later murdered in 1290 by a Khalji chief'.

wars.name: Iltutmish's war with Yildiz of Ghazni
wars.outcome: Iltutmish wins at Tarain on 25 January 1216; Yildiz is captured and later killed at Badaun.

wars.name: Iltutmish's war with Qabacha of Multan

union.text: Multan and Uch

wars.outcome: Qabacha defeated: Uch falls on 4 May 1228, he drowns on 26 May; Multan and Uch under Iltutmish's governors.
wars.note: The Punjab changed hands between the two (Iltutmish took Lahore in the winter of 1216-1217, Qabacha regained it, undated).

wars.name: Conquest of Bengal

zones.text: Lakhnauti (Gaur), the Rarh and Varendra country of the old Sena kingdom

wars.outcome: Tribute in 1225; Lakhnauti captured and Ghiyasuddin Iwaz executed in 1227; Balkha Khalji rebels in 1229 and is defeated in 1230.

wars.name: Iltutmish's campaigns in Rajasthan and Malwa
wars.outcome: Ranthambore 1226, Mandore 1227, Gwalior 12 December 1232 captured; Bhilsa and Ujjain raided in 1234-1235 without annexation.

wars.name: Mongol invasions of Punjab and Sindh
wars.outcome: Jalal ad-Din Mangburni defeated by Genghis Khan at the Indus in 1221 and flees to the Punjab (Iltutmish refuses him refuge); the Mongols raise a siege at Uch in 1246 (Balban) and sack Lahore in Bahram's reign (1240-1242); Prince Muhammad is killed on 9 March 1285. The sultanate keeps the Punjab on the Cliopatria shape.
wars.note: The Delhi Sultanate page says only that the sultanate 'repel[led] attacks by the Mongols', with no dates; the war entry combines the Iltutmish, Balban and Mamluk pages.

wars.name: Bengal revolt of Tughral Tughan Khan
wars.outcome: Two Delhi armies fail; Balban invades Bengal himself in 1281 and kills Tughral; Bughra Khan is put in charge of Bengal and declares independence in 1287.
wars.note: End year not on the page.

wars.name: Khalji Revolution
wars.outcome: Jalal ud-Din Firuz Khalji ends the Mamluk dynasty (1 February to 13 June 1290); no territory changes hands.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey frontier exists on the pages; the Punjab frontier with the Mongols, the Rajput marches and Bengal are approximate throughout.

notes:
Cliopatria's Mamluk row (1210-1293) is the Delhi Mamluks (the Cairo Mamluk Sultanate is a different state with Cliopatria Name 'Mamluk Sultanate'); the dossier starts in 1206 (not 1210) and ends in 1290 (not 1293), with new keyframes for 1206-1209 (which Cliopatria gives to the Ghurids), for 1228 and 1232 (Multan, Gwalior arrive eight and four years before Cliopatria's 1236 shape) and for 1287-1290 (Bengal gone). Pages opened: 5 of 5 (Mamluk dynasty, Qutb ud-Din Aibak, Iltutmish, Delhi Sultanate, Balban). NOT SETTLED: (1) the Punjab 1210-1216 (Lahore was Aibak's seat, then retaken by Iltutmish in the winter of 1216-17 from a holder the page does not name, and Qabacha 'later regained' it) is drawn whole as in Cliopatria; (2) the Mongol frontier on the Indus and Beas (the Delhi Sultanate and Balban pages are silent on 1241 and on Lahore; one page gives Lahore's sack only 'during Bahram's reign'); (3) the 1250-1260 growth of 48k km2 and the Malwa, Chittor and Chhattisgarh parts of the 1236 shape rest on no page opened; (4) the Tughral revolt (the Balban page says 1275 and gives no end year; the end is 1281 on the Tughral Tughan Khan page); (5) the 1229 investiture by the Abbasid caliph al-Mustansir ('recognized Iltutmish's authority in 1228; the embassy arrived in Delhi on 18 February 1229') (now in the ledger: vassal_start 1229 / vassal_end 1258, abbasid-caliphate should move its 1210 start to 1229) belongs to Cliopatria's relation row 'Allegiance of Delhi Sultanate to Abbasid Caliphate' (1210..1259) and the abbasid-caliphate dossier, not to territory here; the row's 1259 end is not on a page opened; (6) the capital: Badaun 1210-1214 (infobox) against 'set up his capital at Delhi' in 1211 (Iltutmish page). States needing dossiers: Qabacha of Multan, Yildiz of Ghazni, the Khalji dynasty of Bengal (Iwaz, 1204-1227), Chahamanas of Ranastambhapura (Ranthambore, a sa-03 slug). Mirrors: ghurid-dynasty carries the 1206 loss to this state; chandela-kingdom, paramara-dynasty and mongol-empire should carry the contests of 1233-34/1247, 1234-35 and 1241-1285. Gazetteer: 'Mandore', 'Ranthambore' and 'Bhilsa' are not in the gazetteer (coordinates used); 'Kalinjar' is a real name the gazetteer lacks and is left as a name.

Repair pass (sa-04-a, 2026-10-19): Bihar now drawn from 1215 (mamluk-dynasty_1215, and added to mamluk-dynasty_1216); Lahore lost to Qabacha in 1211 (Iltutmish page) and drawn without Lahore 1211-1215 (mamluk-dynasty_1211, _1215); Bhilsa an occupation 1234-1239, Ujjain a raid; Odia contest 1243-1247 and occupation 1244-1247 of Rarh and Gauda added (source Narasingha Deva I, not the Eastern Ganga dynasty page, which lacks the years); Abbasid investiture 1229 added; 1287 Bengal counterpart is Bughra Khan's Bengal, successor slug balbani-sultanate-of-bengal.

Thin findings tried (sa-04-a repair): Tughral revolt end 1281 (Tughral page); Lahore sack dated 30 December 1241 (Mongol invasions page); Lahore 1211 (Iltutmish page) already added. Not tried: the Malwa, Chittor and Chhattisgarh parts of the 1236 shape and the 1250 growth (Nasiruddin_Mahmud page).
